title.zh: 卷十三 列傳第七: 徐世譜 魯悉達 周敷 荀朗 周炅
title.en: Volume 13: Xu Shipu; Lu Xida; Zhou Fu; Xun Lang; Zhou Jiong
title.raw: 卷十三 列傳第七: 徐世譜 魯悉達 周敷 荀朗 周炅 Volume 13: Xu Shipu; Lu Xida; Zhou Fu; Xun Lang; Zhou Jiong

sentences.zh: 陳書卷十三

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 13
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 13

sentences.zh: 列傳第七

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Seven
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Seven

sentences.zh: 徐世譜 魯悉達 周敷 荀朗 子法尚 周炅

translations.literal: Xu Shipu; Lu Xida; Zhou Fu; Xun Lang; son Fashang; Zhou Jiong
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shipu; Lu Xida; Zhou Fu; Xun Lang; son Fashang; Zhou Jiong

sentences.zh: 徐世譜

translations.literal: Xu Shipu
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shipu

sentences.zh: 徐世譜字興宗，巴東魚復人也。

translations.literal: Xu Shipu, styled Xingzong, was a native of Yufu in Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shipu, styled Xingzong, came from Yufu in Badong.

sentences.zh: 世居荊州，為主帥，征伐蠻、蜒。

translations.literal: For generations the family dwelt in Jingzhou as a territorial commander, campaigning against the Man and the Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long held Jingzhou as local commanders, campaigning against the Man and Yi peoples.

sentences.zh: 至世譜，尤敢勇有膂力，善水戰。

translations.literal: By Shipu's time he was especially daring and brave, with great physical strength, and skilled in naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Shipu was bolder and stronger than his forebears and excelled at river fighting.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝之為荊州刺史，世譜將領鄉人事焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was governor of Jingzhou, Shipu led the local commanders and village heads in serving him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang governed Jingzhou, Shipu led the district commanders and village heads in his service.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，因預征討，累遷至員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he took part in the punitive campaigns and rose in succession to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he joined the punitive armies and rose step by step to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋領水軍，從司徒陸法和討景，與景戰於赤亭湖。

translations.literal: Soon he took command of the navy and, following Minister of Education Lu Fahe, campaigned against Jing, fighting him at Red Pavilion Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he commanded the navy and, under Minister of Education Lu Fahe, marched against Jing and fought him at Red Pavilion Lake.

sentences.zh: 時景軍甚盛，世譜乃別造樓船、拍艦、火舫、水車以益軍勢。

translations.literal: At that time Jing's army was very strong; Shipu thereupon had tower ships, battering ships, fire vessels, and water-wheels built separately to strengthen the fleet.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's army was then overwhelming. Shipu had new tower ships, rams, fire-boats, and water-engines built to swell his fleet.

sentences.zh: 將戰，又乘大艦居前，大敗景軍，生擒景將任約，景退走。

translations.literal: As battle was joined he again took a great war-ship to the fore, inflicted a great defeat on Jing's army, captured Jing's general Ren Yue alive, and Jing fled.
translations.idiomatic: When battle came he again put a great ship in the van, crushed Jing's army, took Jing's general Ren Yue alive, and drove Jing off.

sentences.zh: 因隨王僧辯攻郢州，世譜復乘大艦臨其倉門，賊將宋子仙據城降。

translations.literal: He then followed Wang Sengbian in attacking Yingzhou; Shipu again took a great war-ship up to the granary gate, and the rebel general Song Zixian surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Sengbian against Yingzhou. Shipu again brought a great ship under the granary gate, and the rebel Song Zixian surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 以功除使持節、信武將軍、信州刺史，封魚復縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed holder of credentials, trustworthy-faith general, and inspector of Xinzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yufu county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made credential-holder, trustworthy-faith general, and inspector of Xinzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yufu with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仍隨僧辯東下，恆為軍鋒。

translations.literal: He still followed Sengbian eastward, always serving as the army's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He still marched east with Sengbian and was always the army's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 又破景將侯子鑒於湖熟。

translations.literal: He again defeated Jing's general Hou Zijian at Hushu.
translations.idiomatic: He again broke Jing's general Hou Zijian at Hushu.

sentences.zh: [1]侯景平後，以功除通直散騎常侍、衡州刺史資，

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 1. After Hou Jing was pacified, for merit he was appointed regular attendant for direct communication, with credentials as inspector of Hengzhou,
translations.idiomatic: [1] After Hou Jing fell, for merit he was made regular attendant for direct communication and given credentials as inspector of Hengzhou,

translations.literal: (garrison)
translations.idiomatic: (garrison)

sentences.zh: 〔領〕河東太守，[2]增邑并前一千戶。

translations.literal: [garrison] Administrator of Hedong, Editorial footnote marker 2. fief increased to one thousand households combined with the former.
translations.idiomatic: [garrison] administrator of Hedong, [2] with his fief raised to one thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 西魏來寇荊州，世譜鎮馬頭岸，據有龍

translations.literal: Western Wei came to raid Jingzhou; Shipu garrisoned Matou Bank and held Long
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei raided Jingzhou, Shipu held Matou Bank and occupied Long

translations.literal: (zhou)
translations.idiomatic: (zhou)

sentences.zh: 〔洲〕，[3]元帝授侍中、使持節、都督江南諸軍事、鎮南將軍、護軍將軍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: [Islet], Editorial footnote marker 3. Emperor Yuan appointed him palace attendant, credential-holder, area commander of all armies south of the Yangzi, general who guards the south, protector-general, and gave him one set of pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: [Islet]. [3] Emperor Yuan made him palace attendant, credential-holder, commander of all armies south of the Yangzi, general who guards the south, and protector-general, with one set of pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷沒，世譜東下依侯瑱。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, Shipu went east and attached himself to Hou Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Shipu went east and joined Hou Zhen.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was transferred to protector-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 2 (558) he was made protector-general.

sentences.zh: 世祖嗣位，加特進，進號安右將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, he was given special advance and promoted to secure-the-right general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was given special advance and promoted to secure-the-right general.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 1 (560) his fief grew by five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為使持節、散騎常侍、都督宣城郡諸軍事、安西將軍、宣城太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: In the second year he went out with credentials as supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, area commander of all military affairs in Xuancheng prefecture, secure-the-west general, and administrator of Xuancheng, salary at the two-thousand-bushel level.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he went out as credential-holder, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of armies in Xuancheng, secure-the-west general, and administrator of Xuancheng at the two-thousand-bushel rank.

sentences.zh: 還為安前將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Returning, he was made secure-the-front general and supernumerary bearer of the left secondary insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was made secure-the-front general and supernumerary bearer of the left secondary insignia.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾失明，謝病不朝。

translations.literal: Soon he went blind from illness and excused himself from court on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon illness blinded him, and he begged leave from court.

sentences.zh: 四年卒，時年五十五。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died, aged fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，諡曰桓侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given his former offices; posthumous name Marquis Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given his former offices, with the posthumous name Marquis Huan.

sentences.zh: 世譜從弟世休，隨世譜自梁征討，亦有戰功。

translations.literal: Shipu's younger cousin Shiuxiu followed Shipu on Liang punitive campaigns and also had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Shipu's younger cousin Shiuxiu followed him on Liang campaigns and won merit in battle.

sentences.zh: 官至員外散騎常侍、安遠將軍，枳縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: He rose to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant and secure-the-distance general, Marquis of Zhi county with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant and secure-the-distance general, Marquis of Zhi with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 光大二年，隸都督淳于量征華皎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangda he served under Area Commander Chunyu Liang in campaigning against Hua Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangda year 2 (567) he served under area commander Chunyu Liang against Hua Jiao.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈通直散騎常侍，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given regular attendant for direct communication; posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made regular attendant for direct communication, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 魯悉達

translations.literal: Lu Xida
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xida

sentences.zh: 魯悉達字志通，扶風郿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Xida, styled Zhitong, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xida, styled Zhitong, came from Mei in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 祖斐，齊通直散騎常侍、安遠將軍、衡州刺史，陽塘侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fei was Liang supernumerary regular attendant for direct communication, secure-the-distance general, inspector of Hengzhou, and Marquis of Yangtang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fei was Liang's supernumerary regular attendant for direct communication, secure-the-distance general, inspector of Hengzhou, and Marquis of Yangtang.

sentences.zh: 父益之，梁雲麾將軍、新蔡義陽二郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Yizhi was Liang cloud-banner general and concurrently administrator of the two commanderies of Xincai and Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yizhi was Liang's cloud-banner general and concurrently administrator of Xincai and Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 悉達幼以孝聞，起家為梁南平嗣王中兵參軍。

translations.literal: From youth Xida was famed for filial piety; he first took office as army supervisor in the establishment of the Prince of Southern Pacification, heir of Liang's Prince of Nangping.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Xida was known for filial piety. He first entered service as army supervisor in the establishment of the Prince of Southern Pacification, heir to Liang's Prince of Nangping.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，悉達糾合鄉人，保新蔡，力田蓄穀。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Xida gathered fellow-townsmen to hold Xincai, farming diligently and storing grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Xida rallied his neighbors to hold Xincai, farmed hard, and stored grain.

sentences.zh: 時兵荒饑饉，京都及上川餓死者十八九，有得存者，皆攜老幼以歸焉。

translations.literal: In that time of military chaos and famine, nine or ten in the capital and upper Yangzi valley died of hunger; those who survived all brought the aged and young back with them.
translations.idiomatic: In the war and famine, eight or nine of ten in the capital and upper Yangzi died of hunger. Those who lived came back with the old and young in tow.

sentences.zh: 悉達分給糧廩，其所濟活者甚眾，仍於新蔡置頓以居之。

translations.literal: Xida distributed grain from his granaries; those he saved were very many, and he then established a camp at Xincai to house them.
translations.idiomatic: Xida opened his granaries. The people he kept alive were countless, and he set a camp at Xincai to shelter them.

sentences.zh: 招集晉熙等五郡，盡有其地。

translations.literal: He recruited the five commanderies including Jinxi and held all their territory.
translations.idiomatic: He drew in five commanderies, including Jinxi, and held all their lands.

sentences.zh: 使其弟廣達領兵隨王僧辯討侯景。

translations.literal: He had his younger brother Guangda lead troops to follow Wang Sengbian in suppressing Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his younger brother Guangda with troops to follow Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 景平，梁元帝授持節、仁威將軍、散騎常侍、北江州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him credential-holder, benevolent-martial general, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and inspector of North Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing fell, Emperor Yuan of Liang made him credential-holder, benevolent-martial general, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and inspector of North Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 悉達雖仗氣任俠，不以富貴驕人，雅好詞賦，招禮才賢，與之賞會。

translations.literal: Though Xida relied on qi and was a knight-errant, he was not proud in wealth and rank; he loved rhapsodies and poems by nature and recruited and treated men of talent, sharing appreciation with them.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lived by bold spirit and the code of the knight-errant, he was never haughty in wealth or rank. He loved verse by nature, gathered men of talent, and feasted with them on their writing.

sentences.zh: 遷安南將軍、吳州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to secure-the-south general and inspector of Wu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to secure-the-south general and inspector of Wu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，哀毀過禮，因遘疾卒，時年三十八。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother; his grief and emaciation exceeded ritual, and he thereupon fell ill and died, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died his grief and wasting went beyond ritual. He fell ill and died, aged thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈安左將軍、江州刺史，諡曰孝侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given secure-the-left general and inspector of Jiangzhou; posthumous name Marquis Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made secure-the-left general and inspector of Jiangzhou, with the posthumous name Marquis Xiao.

sentences.zh: 子覽嗣。

translations.literal: His son Lan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 弟廣達，別有傳。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guangda has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guangda has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 周敷字仲遠，臨川人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu, styled Zhongyuan, was a native of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu, styled Zhongyuan, came from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 為郡豪族。

translations.literal: His clan was a great family of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was a great house of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 敷形貌眇小，如不勝衣，而膽力勁果，超出時輩。

translations.literal: Fu's looks were slight and small, as if he could not bear his clothes, yet his courage and strength were fierce and resolute, surpassing men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was slight of build, as if his clothes weighed him down, yet his courage and force were fierce, beyond his peers.

sentences.zh: 性豪俠，輕財重士，鄉黨少年任氣者咸歸之。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold and chivalrous, light with wealth and heavy with scholars; young men of the village who trusted in bold spirit all joined him.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and chivalrous by nature, careless of money and devoted to men of worth. Every hot-blooded youth in the district rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，鄉人周續合徒眾以討賊為名，梁內史始興藩王蕭毅以郡讓續，[6]續所部內有欲侵掠於毅，敷擁護之，親率其黨捍衛，送至豫章。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the townsman Zhou Xu gathered a host under the name of suppressing bandits; Liang's interior secretary the Prince of Shixing Xiao Yi made over the commandery to Xu, Editorial footnote marker 6. and within Xu's command some wished to plunder Yi; Fu guarded him, personally leading his faction to defend and escort him to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion the townsman Zhou Xu raised men in the name of punishing rebels. Liang's interior secretary, Prince of Shixing Xiao Yi, yielded the commandery to Xu. [6] Some of Xu's men meant to plunder Yi. Fu shielded him, led his own band in defense, and saw him safely to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 時觀寧侯蕭永、長樂侯蕭基、豐城侯蕭泰避難流寓，聞敷信義，皆往依之。

translations.literal: At that time the Marquis of Guanning Xiao Yong, the Marquis of Changle Xiao Ji, and the Marquis of Fengcheng Xiao Tai were refugees in flight; hearing of Fu's trustworthiness and righteousness they all went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Guanning Xiao Yong, the Marquis of Changle Xiao Ji, and the Marquis of Fengcheng Xiao Tai were then refugees. Hearing of Fu's faith and honor, they all came to him.

sentences.zh: 敷愍其危懼，屈體崇敬，厚加給卹，送之西上。

translations.literal: Fu pitied their peril and fear, bowed his body in reverence, gave them generous relief, and sent them upriver west.
translations.idiomatic: Fu pitied their fear, treated them with humble courtesy, gave them generous aid, and sent them west upriver.

sentences.zh: 俄而續部下將帥爭權，復反，殺續以降周迪。

translations.literal: Before long Xu's subordinate commanders vied for power, rebelled again, killed Xu, and surrendered to Zhou Di.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xu's officers fought for power, rebelled again, killed Xu, and submitted to Zhou Di.

sentences.zh: 迪素無簿閥，恐失眾心，倚敷族望，深求交結。

translations.literal: Di by nature had no register of lineage and feared losing the hearts of the masses; relying on Fu's clan prestige he sought his friendship deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Di had no pedigree in the registers and feared losing the crowd. He leaned on Fu's family standing and courted him hard.

sentences.zh: 敷未能自固，事迪甚恭，迪大憑仗之，漸有兵眾。

translations.literal: Fu could not yet secure himself and served Di with great deference; Di leaned heavily on him and gradually had troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Fu could not yet stand alone and served Di with deep deference. Di relied on him heavily and slowly built an army.

sentences.zh: 迪據臨川之工塘，敷鎮臨川故郡。

translations.literal: Di held Gongtang in Linchuan; Fu garrisoned the old commandery seat of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Di held Gongtang in Linchuan; Fu held the old commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，梁元帝授敷使持節、通直散騎常侍、信武將軍、寧州刺史，封西豐縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed Fu credential-holder, regular attendant for direct communication, trustworthy-faith general, and inspector of Ningzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing fell, Emperor Yuan of Liang made Fu credential-holder, regular attendant for direct communication, trustworthy-faith general, and inspector of Ningzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，王琳據有上流，余孝頃與琳黨李

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi; Yu Xiaoxiang with Lin's partisan Li
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi. Yu Xiaoxiang with Lin's ally Li

translations.literal: (Xi)
translations.idiomatic: (Xi)

sentences.zh: 〔孝〕欽等共圍周迪，[7]敷大致人馬以助於迪。

translations.literal: [Xiao] Qin and others jointly besieged Zhou Di, Editorial footnote marker 7. and Fu gathered a great force of men and horses to aid Di.
translations.idiomatic: [Xiao] Qin and others besieged Zhou Di together. [7] Fu mustered a great body of men and horses to help Di.

sentences.zh: 迪擒孝頃等，敷功居多。

translations.literal: Di captured Xiaoxiang and the others; Fu's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Di took Xiaoxiang and his fellows prisoner. Fu's share of the merit was greatest.

sentences.zh: 熊曇朗之殺周文育，據豫章，將兵萬餘人襲敷，徑至城下，敷與戰，大敗之，追奔五十餘里，曇朗單馬獲免，盡收其軍實。

translations.literal: Xiong Tanlang killed Zhou Wenyü, held Yuzhang, and with more than ten thousand troops raided Fu, coming straight to the foot of the walls; Fu fought him and inflicted a great defeat, pursued more than fifty li; Tanlang escaped on a single horse and all his military stores were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tanlang killed Zhou Wenyü, held Yuzhang, and struck Fu with more than ten thousand men, coming straight to the walls. Fu fought him, routed him, and chased him fifty li. Tanlang escaped on one horse; all his stores fell to Fu.

sentences.zh: 曇朗走巴山郡，收合餘黨，敷因與周迪、黃法𣰋等進兵圍曇朗，屠之。

translations.literal: Tanlang fled to Bashan commandery and gathered the remnant party; Fu then with Zhou Di, Huang Faqu, and others advanced to surround Tanlang and slaughtered them.
translations.idiomatic: Tanlang fled to Bashan commandery and rallied the remnants. Fu then marched with Zhou Di, Huang Faqu, and others, surrounded Tanlang, and slaughtered his force.

sentences.zh: 王琳平，授散騎常侍、平西將軍、豫章太守。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified he was appointed supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-west general, and administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin fell he was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-west general, and administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 是時南江酋帥並顧戀巢窟，私署令長，不受召，朝廷未遑致討，但羈縻之，唯敷獨先入朝。

translations.literal: At that time southern river chieftains all clung to their nests and caves, privately appointing magistrates and heads and not answering summonses; the court had not yet leisure to punish them but only kept them on leashes—only Fu alone first entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Southern chieftains still clung to their hill nests, appointing their own magistrates and ignoring summons. The court had no leisure to punish them and could only hold them on a loose rein—only Fu came to court first.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，詣闕，進號安西將軍，給鼓吹一部，賜以女樂一部，[8]令還鎮豫章。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he came to the palace; his title was advanced to secure-the-west general and he was given one set of pipes and drums and a set of female musicians, Editorial footnote marker 8. with orders to return and hold Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 2 (561) he came to the capital. His title rose to secure-the-west general; he was given pipes and drums and a troupe of female musicians, [8] and ordered back to hold Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 周迪以敷素出己下，超致顯貴，深不平、乃舉兵反，遣弟方興以兵襲敷。

translations.literal: Zhou Di because Fu had always ranked below him yet now surged to high honor was deeply resentful; he thereupon raised troops in rebellion and sent his younger brother Fangxing with an army to raid Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Di had always outranked Fu, and Fu's sudden rise bred deep resentment. Di rebelled and sent his brother Fangxing to raid Fu.

sentences.zh: 敷與戰，大破方興。

translations.literal: Fu fought him and inflicted a great defeat on Fangxing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu met him in battle and broke Fangxing completely.

sentences.zh: 仍率眾從都督吳明徹攻迪，破之，擒其弟方興并諸渠帥。

translations.literal: He then led his host to follow Area Commander Wu Mingche in attacking Di, routed him, and captured his younger brother Fangxing together with the various chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed area commander Wu Mingche against Di, routed him, and took Fangxing and the other chieftains prisoner.

sentences.zh: 詔以敷為安西將軍、臨川太守，餘並如故。

translations.literal: An edict made Fu secure-the-west general and administrator of Linchuan; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him secure-the-west general and administrator of Linchuan; his other honors stood.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為使持節、都督南豫北江二州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、南豫州刺史，增邑五百戶，常侍、鼓吹如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned with credentials as area commander of military affairs in the two provinces of South Yu and North Jiang, general who guards the south, and inspector of South Yu, fief increased by five hundred households; regular attendant and pipes and drums unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as credential-holder, commander of armies in South Yu and North Jiang, general who guards the south, and inspector of South Yu, with five hundred more households. His attendant rank and pipes and drums were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 五年，迪又收合餘眾，還襲東興。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Di again gathered remnant masses and returned to raid Dongxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Di rallied his remnants and struck Dongxing again.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣都督章昭達征迪，敷又從軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda to campaign against Di; Fu again followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent area commander Zhang Zhaoda against Di, and Fu marched again.

sentences.zh: 至定川縣，與迪相對。

translations.literal: Reaching Dingchuan county, he faced Di across the line.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingchuan county he faced Di across the line.

sentences.zh: 迪紿敷曰：「吾昔與弟戮力同心，宗從匪他，豈規相害。

translations.literal: Di deceived Fu, saying: "Formerly I and you, my younger brother, strove together with one heart; we are clan kin and no others—how could I scheme to harm you?
translations.idiomatic: Di tricked Fu, saying: "Once we fought side by side, you and I, as kin and not strangers. How could I mean you harm?

sentences.zh: 今願伏罪還朝，因弟披露心腑，先乞挺身共立盟誓。

translations.literal: Now I wish to confess guilt and return to court; through you, younger brother, I disclose my inmost heart; first I beg to bare my body and stand together to swear an oath."
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to confess and return to court. Through you, younger brother, I lay bare my heart. First let us stand together and swear an oath."

sentences.zh: 」敷許之，方登壇，為迪所害，時年三十五。

translations.literal: Fu agreed; as he was mounting the altar he was killed by Di, aged thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Fu agreed. As he climbed the altar, Di killed him. He was thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「使持節、散騎常侍、都督南豫州緣江諸軍事、鎮南將軍、南豫州刺史西豐縣開國侯敷，受任遐征，淹時違律，虛衿姦詭，遂貽喪仆。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Credential-holder, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, area commander of all armies along the Yangzi bank of South Yu, general who guards the south, inspector of South Yu, Opening Marquis of Xifeng county Fu—charged with a distant expedition, he long disobeyed regulations, held an empty breast toward treacherous deceit, and so met death and fell.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Fu, credential-holder, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of armies along the South Yu Yangzi bank, general who guards the south, inspector of South Yu, and Opening Marquis of Xifeng—sent on a distant campaign, he long broke discipline, opened his heart to treachery, and so met death in the field.

sentences.zh: [9]但夙著勤誠，亟勞戎旅，猶深惻愴，愍悼于懷。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 9. Yet from of old he showed loyal earnestness and repeatedly labored on campaign; We are still deeply moved to compassion and grieve in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: [9] Yet he had long shown loyal service and toil on campaign. We are still deeply moved and grieve in Our heart.

sentences.zh: 可存其茅賦，量所賻卹，還葬京邑。

translations.literal: His feudal income may be preserved; measure out funeral gifts as due and return his body for burial in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Let his fief be kept. Give funeral gifts as fitting and bring his body back for burial in the capital."

sentences.zh: 」諡曰脫。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name Tuo.

sentences.zh: 子智安嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 敷兄彖，共敷據本鄉，亦授臨川太守。

translations.literal: Fu's elder brother Juan together with Fu held their home district and was also appointed administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's elder brother Juan had held their home district with him and was also made administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 荀朗字深明，潁川潁陰人也。

translations.literal: Xun Lang, styled Shenming, was a native of Yingyin in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Lang, styled Shenming, came from Yingyin in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 祖延祖，梁潁川太守，父伯道，衛尉卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan'zu was Liang administrator of Yingchuan; his father Bodao was minister of court ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan'zu was Liang's administrator of Yingchuan; his father Bodao was minister of court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 朗少慷慨，有將帥大略，起家梁廬陵王行參軍。

translations.literal: From youth Lang was generous and bold, with the grand strategy of a commander; he first took office as traveling attendant in the establishment of Liang's Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Lang was open-handed and bold, with a commander's breadth of plan. He first served as traveling attendant in the establishment of Liang's Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，朗招率徒旅，據巢湖閒，無所屬。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Lang gathered a following, held the lands about Chaohu Lake, and belonged to no one.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Lang gathered followers, held the country about Chaohu Lake, and owed allegiance to no one.

sentences.zh: 臺城陷後，簡文帝密詔授朗雲麾將軍、豫州刺史，令與外藩討景。

translations.literal: After the Terrace City fell Emperor Jianwen of Liang sent a secret edict appointing Lang cloud-banner general and inspector of Yu and ordering him with outer provinces to suppress Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell, Emperor Jianwen of Liang secretly made him cloud-banner general and inspector of Yu and ordered him, with the outer provinces, to crush Jing.

sentences.zh: 景使儀同宋子仙、任約等頻往征之，朗據山立砦自守，子仙不能克。

translations.literal: Jing sent comrades-in-arms Song Zixian, Ren Yue, and others repeatedly to campaign against him; Lang held mountain stockades in defense and Zixian could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent his comrades Song Zixian, Ren Yue, and others against him again and again. Lang held mountain forts and Zixian could not take him.

sentences.zh: 時京師大饑，百姓皆於江外就食，朗更招致部曲，解衣推食，以相賑贍，眾至數萬人。

translations.literal: At that time the capital had great famine; commoners all went south of the Yangzi to seek food; Lang further recruited followers, doffed his own garments and shared food, giving mutual relief, until his following reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was starving. People crossed the Yangzi to find food. Lang gathered more men, stripped off his own clothes to feed them, and built a following of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 侯景敗於巴陵，朗出自濡須截景，破其後軍。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was defeated at Baling Lang came out from Ruru Ford to intercept Jing and broke his rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was beaten at Baling, Lang came out from Ruru Ford, cut Jing off, and smashed his rearguard.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯東討，朗遣其將范寶勝及弟曉領兵二千助之。

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian campaigned east; Lang sent his general Fan Baosheng and his younger brother Xiao each to lead two thousand troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian marched east, Lang sent his general Fan Baosheng and his younger brother Xiao, each with two thousand men, to help.

sentences.zh: 侯景平後，又別破齊將郭元建於踟躕山。

translations.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified he again separately defeated Qi general Guo Yuanjian at Chichu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing fell he again defeated Qi general Guo Yuanjian at Chichu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 梁承聖二年，率部曲萬餘家濟江，入宣城郡界立頓。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng of Liang, [Lang] led more than ten thousand households of his following across the Yangzi, entered Xuancheng commandery territory, and established a camp.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Chengsheng year two, Lang led more than ten thousand follower households across the Yangzi, entered Xuancheng commandery, and set up camp.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝授朗持節、通直散騎常侍、安南將軍、都督南兗州諸軍事、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed Lang Bearer of the Staff, Courier Direct-Communication Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Pacifying-South General, Area Commander over Military Affairs in South Yanzhou, and Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang made Lang bearer of the staff, courier direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-south general, commander of South Yanzhou armies, and inspector of the province.

sentences.zh: 未行而荊州陷。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, Jingzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, Jingzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 子法尚

translations.literal: Son Fa Shang
translations.idiomatic: Son Fa Shang

sentences.zh: 法尚少俶儻，有文武幹略，起家江寧令，襲爵興寧縣侯。

translations.literal: Fa Shang in youth was unrestrained and bold, possessed civil and military capacity and strategy; he began his career as magistrate of Jiangning and inherited enfeoffment as Marquis of Xingning county.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Shang as a youth was bold and enterprising, with both civil and military talent; he began as magistrate of Jiangning and inherited the marquisate of Xingning.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，隨吳明徹北伐。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he followed Wu Mingche on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year five he joined Wu Mingche's northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋授通直散騎侍郎，除涇令，歷梁、安城太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was given Courier Direct-Communication Scattered-Cavalry Gentleman, dismissed as magistrate of Jing, and successively served as Administrator of Liang and Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made courier direct-communication scattered-cavalry gentleman, relieved as magistrate of Jing, and served in turn as administrator of Liang and Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 禎明中，為都督郢巴武三州諸軍事、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Zhenming era he was made Area Commander over Military Affairs in the three prefectures of Ying, Ba, and Wu, and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenming he was made commander of armies in Ying, Ba, and Wu and inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及隋軍濟江，法尚降于漢東道元帥秦王。

translations.literal: When Sui forces crossed the Yangzi, Fa Shang surrendered to the Prince of Qin, commander of the Handong route.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui army crossed the Yangzi, Fa Shang surrendered to the Prince of Qin, commander on the Handong route.

sentences.zh: 入隋，歷邵、觀、綿、豐四州刺史，巴東、燉煌二郡太守。

translations.literal: Entering Sui service, he successively was Inspector of the four prefectures Shao, Guan, Mian, and Feng, and Administrator of the two commanderies Badong and Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served in turn as inspector of Shao, Guan, Mian, and Feng and as administrator of Badong and Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 周炅字文昭，汝南安成人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Jiong, style name Wenzhao, was a native of Ancheng in Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jiong, courtesy name Wenzhao, was from Ancheng in Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 祖彊，齊太子舍人、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiang was Qi Crown Prince's Household Attendant and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiang had been crown prince's household attendant under Qi and inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父靈起，梁通直散騎常侍、廬桂二州刺史，保城縣侯。

translations.literal: His father Lingqi was Liang Courier Direct-Communication Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and Inspector of the two prefectures Lu and Gui, Marquis of Baocheng county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingqi was Liang courier direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant and inspector of Lu and Gui, marquis of Baocheng county.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，王琳擁據上流，炅以州從之。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi; Jiong followed him with his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi, and Jiong brought his province to his side.

sentences.zh: 及王琳遣其將曹慶等攻周迪，仍使炅將兵掎角而進，為侯安都所敗，擒炅送都。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin sent his generals Cao Qing and others to attack Zhou Di, he also had Jiong lead troops in pincer advance; [Jiong] was defeated by Hou Andu, captured, and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin sent Cao Qing and others against Zhou Di, he also ordered Jiong to advance in concert; Hou Andu defeated him, took him prisoner, and sent him to court.

sentences.zh: 世祖釋炅，授戎威將軍、定州刺史，帶西陽、武昌二郡太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen released Jiong and appointed him Martial-Power General and Inspector of Dingzhou, concurrently Administrator of the two commanderies Xiyang and Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen freed Jiong and made him martial-power general and inspector of Dingzhou, with concurrent charge of Xiyang and Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，留異據東陽反，世祖召炅還都，欲令討異。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjia, Liu Yi held Dongyang in rebellion; Emperor Wen summoned Jiong back to the capital, intending to have him campaign against Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year two Liu Yi rebelled at Dongyang; Emperor Wen recalled Jiong to the capital to lead the campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 未至而異平，炅還本鎮。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Yi was pacified; Jiong returned to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Yi had been suppressed, and Jiong returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，預平華皎之功，授員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he shared in the merit of pacifying Hua Jiao and was given Supernumerary Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiankang year one he shared credit for suppressing Hua Jiao and was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，遷持節、龍驤將軍、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Dragon-Prancing General, and Courier Direct-Communication Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year one he was made bearer of the staff, dragon-prancing general, and courier direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 五年，進授使持節、西道都督安蘄江衡司定六州諸軍事、安州刺史，改封龍源縣侯，增邑并前一千戶。

translations.literal: In year five he was advanced to Bearer of the Staff with full credentials, Western Route Area Commander over Military Affairs in the six prefectures An, Qi, Jiang, Heng, Si, and Ding, and Inspector of Anzhou; his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Longyuan county, fief increased together with the former to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he was promoted to full bearer of the staff, western-route commander of armies in An, Qi, Jiang, Heng, Si, and Ding, and inspector of Anzhou; his title was changed to marquis of Longyuan, with fief raised to one thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 其年隨都督吳明徹北討，所向克捷，一月之中，獲十二城。

translations.literal: That year he followed Area Commander Wu Mingche on the northern campaign; wherever he went he was victorious, and within one month he took twelve cities.
translations.idiomatic: That year he followed Wu Mingche north; he carried every assault and took twelve cities in a month.

sentences.zh: 齊遣尚書左丞陸騫以眾二萬出自巴、蘄，與炅相遇。

translations.literal: Qi sent Left Assistant in the Department of State Affairs Lu Qian with twenty thousand men out from Ba and Qi; he encountered Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Lu Qian, left assistant in the department of state affairs, with twenty thousand men from Ba and Qi, and he met Jiong.

sentences.zh: 炅留羸弱輜重，設疑兵以當之，身率精銳，由間道邀其後，大敗騫軍，虜獲器械馬驢，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Jiong left the weak and the baggage train, set decoy troops to face them, and personally led picked warriors by a bypath to strike their rear; he inflicted a great defeat on Qian's army and captured weapons, horses, and mules beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong left the weak and the baggage, posted decoys to hold them, and led picked men by a hidden route to strike their rear; he routed Qian's army and seized arms, horses, and mules beyond count.

sentences.zh: 進攻巴州，克之。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Bazhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked and captured Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 於是江北諸城及穀陽士民，並誅渠帥以城降。

translations.literal: Thereupon the cities north of the Yangzi and the gentry and people of Guyang all executed their chieftains and surrendered their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Then the cities north of the river and the people of Guyang killed their leaders and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進號和戎將軍、散騎常侍，增邑并前一千五百戶。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Harmonizes with the Rong and Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant; fief increased together with the former to one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who harmonizes with the Rong and scattered-cavalry regular attendant, with fief raised to one thousand five hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 仍敕追炅入朝。

translations.literal: An edict then recalled Jiong to court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then recalled him to court.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭詧定州刺史田龍升以城降，詔以為振遠將軍、定州刺史，封赤亭王。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Cha's Inspector of Dingzhou Tian Longsheng had surrendered his city;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tian Longsheng, inspector of Dingzhou under Xiao Cha, had surrendered his city;

sentences.zh: 及炅入朝，龍升以江北六州七鎮叛入于齊，齊遣歷陽王高景安帥師應之。

translations.literal: when Jiong entered court, Longsheng rebelled with the six prefectures and seven garrisons north of the Yangzi and went over to Qi; Qi sent the Prince of Liyang, Gao Jing'an, to lead troops to support him.
translations.idiomatic: but when Jiong came to court, Longsheng rebelled with six prefectures and seven garrisons north of the river and defected to Qi, which sent Prince Jing'an of Liyang with an army to aid him.

sentences.zh: 於是令炅為江北道大都督，總統眾軍，以討龍升。

translations.literal: Thereupon [the court] made Jiong Grand Commander of the Northern Yangzi Route, commanding all armies, to campaign against Longsheng.
translations.idiomatic: The court then made Jiong grand commander on the northern Yangzi route and gave him all armies to crush Longsheng.

sentences.zh: 龍升使弋陽太守田龍琰率眾二萬陣於亭川，高景安於水陵、陰山為其聲援，龍升引軍別營山谷。

translations.literal: Longsheng sent Yiyang Administrator Tian Longyan with twenty thousand men to form battle lines at Tingchuan; Gao Jing'an at Shuiling and Yinshan gave him vocal support; Longsheng led troops to encamp separately in the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Longsheng sent Tian Longyan, administrator of Yiyang, with twenty thousand men to line up at Tingchuan; Gao Jing'an backed him from Shuiling and Yinshan; Longsheng camped apart in the hills.

sentences.zh: 炅乃分兵各當其軍，身率驍勇先擊龍升，龍升大敗，龍琰望塵而奔，並追斬之，高景安遁走，盡復江北之地。

translations.literal: Jiong then divided his troops to face each army, personally led his champions in the first strike on Longsheng, and inflicted a great defeat; Longyan fled at the sight of dust and both were pursued and beheaded; Gao Jing'an fled; he fully recovered the territory north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong split his force to hold each enemy host, led his champions in a first blow on Longsheng, and routed him; Longyan fled at the dust and both were run down and killed; Gao Jing'an escaped; and the whole north bank was recovered.

sentences.zh: 以功增邑并前二千戶，進號平北將軍，定州刺史，持節、都督如故，仍賜女妓一部。

translations.literal: For merit fief was increased together with the former to two thousand households; his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Dingzhou, bearer of the staff and area command unchanged; he was also granted a troupe of female entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: For merit his fief rose to two thousand households in all; he was made general who pacifies the north and inspector of Dingzhou, keeping staff and command; and he received a troupe of female entertainers.

sentences.zh: 太建八年卒官，時年六十四。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taijian he died in office, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year eight he died in office at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈司州刺史，封武昌郡公，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Inspector of Sizhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuchang commandery, posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Sizhou and duke of Wuchang commandery, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子法僧嗣，官至宣城太守。

translations.literal: His son Faseng succeeded him and reached the post of Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Faseng succeeded him and rose to administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：彼數子者，或驅馳前代，或擁據故鄉，並識運知歸，因機景附，位升列牧，爵致通侯，美矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Those several men either galloped through earlier ages or held their native districts; all recognized the turn of fortune, attached themselves as opportunity arose, rose to rank as regional governors, and enfeoffment reached full marquis—magnificent indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: These men either rode the currents of an earlier age or held their home country; each saw where fortune was turning, joined at the right moment, rose to govern provinces, and won marquisates—how splendid.

sentences.zh: 昔張耳、陳餘自同於至戚，周敷、周迪亦誓等暱親，尋鋒刃而誅殘，斯甚夫胡越矣。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhang Er and Chen Yu were as close as the nearest kin; Zhou Fu and Zhou Di likewise swore bonds like intimate relatives—yet soon they turned blades and slaughtered one another; this was even more extreme than Hu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Er and Chen Yu stood as close as kin; Zhou Fu and Zhou Di swore the same kind of bond—yet they soon drew blades on each other, a breach worse than between Hu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 讎隙因於勢利，何其鄙歟？

translations.literal: Enmity arose from power and profit—how base!
translations.idiomatic: Their feud grew from rank and gain—how base!

translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 又破景將侯子鑒於湖熟 按「湖熟」當作「姑孰」。

translations.literal: Again defeated Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian at Hushu—Comment: "Hushu" should read "Gudu."
translations.idiomatic: On again defeating Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian at Hushu: Hushu should read Gudu.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承聖元年，王僧辯等破侯景將侯子鑒於姑孰，見《梁書·侯景傳》及《通鑑》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengsheng of Liang, Wang Sengbian and others defeated Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian at Gudu—see the Liang History biography of Hou Jing and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Chengsheng year one Wang Sengbian and others defeated Hou Zijian at Gudu; see the Liang History biography of Hou Jing and the Comprehensive Mirror.

translations.idiomatic: [Concurrently] administrator of Hedong—emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按錢大昕《廿二史考異》云：「『鎮』當作『領』。

translations.literal: Comment: Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories says: "'zhen' should read 'ling.'
translations.idiomatic: Note: Qian Daxin writes in his Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories: zhen should read ling.

sentences.zh: 梁、陳之間，往往有以刺史資領郡守、縣令者。」

translations.literal: Between Liang and Chen it was common for men to hold the salary of inspector while concurrently serving as commandery administrator or county magistrate."
translations.idiomatic: Between Liang and Chen it was common to hold inspector's salary while concurrently governing a commandery or county."

sentences.zh: 〔洲〕據《南史》改。

translations.literal: [Islet]—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: [Islet]—emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按《讀史方輿紀要》七八，荊州府江陵縣有龍洲，在府西南十六里江中。

translations.literal: Comment: Essentials of Historical Geography 78 says that in Jiangling county of Jingzhou prefecture there was Long Islet, in the river sixteen li southwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Essentials of Historical Geography 78 places Long Islet in the river sixteen li southwest of Jiangling, seat of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 留異余孝頃周迪等所在鋒起 「鋒起」各本作「蜂起」，《南史》、《元龜》四一二同。

translations.literal: Where Liu Yi, Yu Xiaoshou, Zhou Di, and others were rising in force—"rising in force" in all editions reads "swarming like bees"; the History of the Southern Dynasties and Yuan Gui 412 the same.
translations.idiomatic: On Liu Yi, Yu Xiaoshou, Zhou Di, and others rising in force: every edition reads swarming like bees; the History of the Southern Dynasties and Yuan Gui 412 agree.

sentences.zh: 按鋒起言一時並起，勢銳不可當也。

translations.literal: Comment: "rising in force" means all rising at once with sharp, irresistible momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Note: rising in force means erupting together with irresistible sharpness.

sentences.zh: 古書「鋒起」「蜂起」往往互出，如《後漢書·光武紀》「寇盜鋒起」，注「『鋒』字或作『蜂』」，即其例也。

translations.literal: In ancient books "rising in force" and "swarming like bees" often interchange, as in the Later Han Annals of Emperor Guangwu, "bandits rose in force," commentary: "the character 'force' is sometimes written 'bee'"—that is the pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient texts often alternate rising in force and swarming like bees, as in the Later Han Annals of Guangwu: bandits rose in force, with a note that force may be written bee—that is the pattern.

sentences.zh: 齊遣行臺慕容紹宗以眾三萬來攻鬱口諸鎮 錢大昕《廿二史考異》云：「按慕容紹宗之死在齊未受禪以前，安得此時尚存。

translations.literal: Qi sent Mobile Headquarters Murong Shaozong with thirty thousand men to attack the garrisons at Yugou—Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories says: "Comment: Murong Shaozong died before Qi received the mandate; how could he still be alive at this time?
translations.idiomatic: On Qi sending Murong Shaozong with thirty thousand men against Yugou: Qian Daxin notes that Shaozong died before Qi received the mandate and could not have been alive here.

sentences.zh: 此史家傳聞之誤，《南史》亦仍舊聞，而未據《北史》以正之。」

translations.literal: This is an error of transmitted report in the historians; the History of the Southern Dynasties also kept the old report and did not correct it by the Northern History."
translations.idiomatic: This is a transmitted error; the History of the Southern Dynasties kept the old tale and did not correct it against the Northern History."

sentences.zh: 梁內史始興藩王蕭毅以郡讓續 錢大昕《廿二史考異》云：「按梁書及南史，始興王憺薨，世子亮嗣，無名『毅』者。

translations.literal: Liang Interior Secretary and Prince of Shixing Xiao Yi yielded the commandery to Zhou Xu—Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories says: "Comment: According to the Liang History and the History of the Southern Dynasties, when Prince Shixing Xiao Dan died his heir Liang succeeded; there is no one named 'Yi.'
translations.idiomatic: On Liang interior secretary and Prince of Shixing Xiao Yi yielding the commandery to Zhou Xu: Qian Daxin notes that the Liang History and History of the Southern Dynasties show Prince Shixing Xiao Dan succeeded by his heir Liang, with no Yi.

sentences.zh: 」張森楷校勘記亦云：「始興王憺嗣子亮于時尚存，不云名毅，未知毅為憺何人也。」

translations.literal: " Zhang Senkai's collation note also says: "Prince Shixing Xiao Dan's heir Liang was still alive at the time; it does not say his name was Yi; it is unknown who Yi was to Dan."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai adds: Prince Shixing Xiao Dan's heir Liang was still alive; the text never names Yi; who Yi was to Dan is unknown."

translations.idiomatic: , the biography of Zhou Di, and the Northern Qi History biography of Wang Lin all read Li Xiaoqin.

sentences.zh: 賜以女樂一部 「樂」各本並作「妓」。

translations.literal: Granted a troupe of female music—"music" in all editions reads "courtesans."
translations.idiomatic: On granted a troupe of female music: every edition reads courtesans for music.

sentences.zh: 「一部」二字原缺，據各本補。

translations.literal: The two characters "one troupe" were originally missing and are supplied from the editions.
translations.idiomatic: The words "one troupe" were missing in the base text and are restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 遂貽喪仆 「仆」原作「什」，版刻之訛，今據《元龜》四五二、五九五改正。

translations.literal: Thus brought death upon himself—"upon himself" was originally written "ten"; a block-print error; now corrected according to Yuan Gui 452 and 595.
translations.idiomatic: On "thus brought death upon himself": "upon himself" was originally written ten, a carving error; emended per Yuan Gui 452 and 595.

sentences.zh: 按北監本、汲本、殿本「仆」作「身」，疑後人妄改。

translations.literal: According to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Palace editions, "upon himself" (pu) was written "body" (shen); probably a later mistaken change.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Palace editions, pu (upon himself) was written shen (body); probably a later mistaken change.
